line: Jung's statements on the mana-personality: the dominant of the collective unconscious that the ego is tempted to take for its own.

sections.title: A dominant of the collective unconscious
sections.line: CW7 ¶374–379: what the mana-personality is, and its historical shape.

quotes.quote: “She” is a mana-personality, a being full of some occult and bewitching quality (mana), endowed with magical knowledge and power.

But the mana-personality is a dominant of the collective unconscious, the well-known archetype of the mighty man in the form of hero, chief, magician, medicine-man, saint, the ruler of men and spirits, the friend of God.

Historically, the mana-personality is always in possession of the secret name, or of some esoteric knowledge, or has the prerogative of a special way of acting—quod licet Jovi, non licet bovi—in a word, it has an individual distinction.

sections.title: The danger of identification
sections.line: CW7 ¶382–390: how the ego becomes a mana-personality, and the warning against it.

quotes.quote: I have never yet seen a fairly advanced development of this kind where at least a temporary identification with the archetype of the mana-personality did not take place.
One must therefore beware of the danger of falling victim to the dominant of the mana-personality.
